title: Jude and the Ember
premise: Xanthe Underhill has spent nine years paying off their family's debt to the Ember Temple by mapping and minding the smuggler roads through Thornfell. When the border wards collapse on the night every star in the sky goes dark, the kingdom of Vaelor ceases to exist in any legal sense—its records burned, its borders sealed, its people declared stateless by neighboring powers. Xanthe discovers that Jude, the temple's quiet lamplighter and Xanthe's secret love, carries an 'ember': a living fragment of the old covenant that can reopen the door out of the vanished country before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. Hunted by wardens of three rival states who each want the ember for themselves, Xanthe must choose between delivering Jude to safety alone or breaking their debt-bond to walk beside them. In the end, Xanthe spends their freedom to hold the door open, Jude kindles the ember into a new border no empire can claim, and the two step through together—not escaping Vaelor, but carrying it with them.
about_author: Rosalind Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing disputed border treaties before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse near real mountain passes, where they keep a lamp burning in the window for travelers without papers.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A routine night guiding a smuggler caravan through Thornfell establishes Xanthe's double life: obedient scribe by day, invisible guide by night, always counting what they owe. The emotional beat is weary competence masking loneliness, deepened by an unspoken moment with Jude at the temple lamps.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The wards fall and the sky empties of stars; Vaelor's capital burns its own archives to prevent seizure. Xanthe races back to the temple through collapsing checkpoints. The beat is vertigo—the maps in Xanthe's head now describe a country that officially does not exist.

chapters.title: What the Lamplighter Carries
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude reveals the ember hidden in their lantern—a fragment of Vaelor's founding covenant—and asks Xanthe to guide them to the Door of Thirteen Turns before the moon completes its cycle. The beat is terrified trust: love confessed sideways, as a request for rescue.

chapters.title: Three Flags on One Road
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The first warden patrol catches them; Xanthe talks their way past using knowledge of all three occupying states' protocols, learning each wants the ember as legitimacy for its claim. The beat is the chilling realization that invisibility is over—Xanthe is now evidence.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Mercy
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The temple's high scribe, holding Xanthe's debt-bond, offers to void it if Jude is surrendered to the northern state. Jude refuses and steals the bond itself. The beat is guilt and resolve: Jude chooses to become a thief for the person who never asked to be saved.

chapters.title: Salt Road, Ash Road
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A brutal crossing of the high passes with refugees who attach themselves to the pair; Xanthe must decide whether the smuggler's code of self-preservation still applies when there is no law left to hide from. The beat is reluctant leadership—belonging arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Remembered
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Captured briefly by a southern warden who turns out to be a former temple student of Jude's; she lets them go but warns that the thirteenth turn brings not escape but judgment. The beat is doubt: is the door salvation, or the country's final accounting?

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. All three states' forces converge on the Door of Thirteen Turns as the moon reaches fullness; the refugee column becomes a shield, and Xanthe openly breaks their debt-bond, declaring themselves free and therefore fully culpable. The beat is defiant clarity.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. At the threshold, the ember demands a price: it will only open for someone who belongs wholly to Vaelor. Xanthe pours their memories of every mapped road into the flame while Jude holds the light steady against the wardens' assault. The beat is sacrifice transmuted into foundation.

chapters.title: A Border Made of Light
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, then shared. The ember becomes a new border drawn around people rather than land; the refugees pass through, the wardens falter before a boundary no treaty recognizes. Xanthe, memory-scoured but alive, relearns Jude's name first. The beat is homecoming: belonging chosen, not granted.
